t: Which of the following is a physical hazard in motor insurance?
o: A vehicle with worn-out brakes and bald tyres
A car dealer who inflates the IDV
An owner who leaves the car unlocked because it is insured
A driver who habitually exaggerates repair bills
e: Physical hazard relates to the tangible condition of the subject matter; the other options are moral or morale hazards.

t: Fire insurance business is defined under which Section of the Insurance Act, 1938?
e: Section 2(6A) defines fire insurance business; Section 2(13A) defines marine insurance business and Section 2(13B) miscellaneous insurance business.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to register as a general insurer in India is:
e: The Insurance Act, 1938 requires ₹100 crore paid-up equity for life, general and health insurers and ₹200 crore for a reinsurer.

t: The 'basis clause' in a proposal form provides that:
o: Premium is payable on a monthly basis
Claims are settled on reinstatement basis
The policy is issued on an agreed value basis
The statements in the proposal form form the basis of the contract and are warranted to be true
e: The basis clause incorporates the proposal into the contract, making the accuracy of answers a condition; regulators now require material misstatement for repudiation rather than trivial inaccuracies.

t: An underwriter's delegated authority is ₹10 crore sum insured per fire risk. A broker submits a proposal with sum insured ₹9 crore but the risk is a fireworks factory, which the underwriting policy lists as a 'referral occupancy'. The underwriter should:
o: Refer the risk to the higher underwriting authority because occupancy-based referral applies regardless of sum insured
Accept, since the sum insured is within authority
Accept subject to reinsurer's consent only
e: Underwriting policies specify referral triggers by both amount and hazard; a listed hazardous occupancy must be referred even if the sum insured is within limit.

t: A 'long-term' policy is one which:
o: Has an indemnity period longer than 12 months
Covers a period exceeding twelve months, often with a discount on the premium
e: Long-term policies (e.g. dwelling fire for several years, long-term motor TP for new vehicles) run for more than one year; the premium is collected upfront and often discounted.

t: The short-period rate scale applies when:
o: A policy is issued for a period of less than twelve months or is cancelled by the insured mid-term
A policy is cancelled by the insurer
A claim is lodged within one month of inception
The sum insured is below ₹1 lakh
e: Short-period scales (higher than pro-rata) protect the insurer against selection against it for brief covers and on insured-initiated cancellations; insurer cancellations are refunded pro-rata.

t: Under the erstwhile fire tariff short-period scale, a policy issued for three months attracted 40% of the annual premium. An insured takes a fire policy on stock for three months with annual rate giving ₹60,000 per annum. The premium charged is:
e: Short-period premium = 40% of ₹60,000 = ₹24,000, which exceeds the pro-rata amount of ₹15,000 for a quarter.

t: When accepting a risk 'subject to survey', the insurer:
o: Must pay all claims even if the survey reveals misrepresentation
Grants cover provisionally and may amend terms or withdraw cover in accordance with the survey findings
Cannot charge any premium until survey
Transfers the risk to the surveyor
e: Acceptance subject to survey is a conditional acceptance; the survey report determines final terms, loadings or warranties.

t: Under which Section of the Insurance Act, 1938 is an insurer prohibited from assuming risk unless the premium is received in advance?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VB requires premium to be received in advance before risk commencement, subject to prescribed exceptions. Section 64UM deals with surveyors and Section 45 with life policies.

t: 'Frequency' and 'severity' in rate making mean respectively:
o: Number of claims per exposure unit and average cost per claim
Number of policies and number of claims
Premium per policy and claims per policy
Number of agents and number of offices
e: Frequency × severity = pure premium per exposure unit; analysing them separately helps diagnose whether rising losses are due to more claims or costlier claims.

t: Which of the following statements about the exposure base chosen for a line of business is INCORRECT?
o: It should be proportional to expected losses
It should be already in use or easy to obtain
It should be practical to measure and verify
It should be easily manipulated by the insured to lower premium
e: A good exposure base must not be easy for the insured to manipulate; the other three are the classical criteria for selecting an exposure base.

t: Trending in rate making is the process of:
o: Adjusting historical losses and exposures to the levels expected during the period the new rates will be in force
e: Because rates apply to future periods, past data must be adjusted for inflation, changes in claim frequency and legal environment.

t: An insurer writes ₹240 crore of premium evenly through the financial year on annual policies. Using the 50% method, the unexpired risk reserve at year end is:
e: The 50% method assumes policies are written evenly, so on average half the premium is unexpired at year end: 50% of ₹240 crore = ₹120 crore.

t: Incurred claims for a year equal:
o: Claims paid minus reinsurance recoveries only
Claims paid during the year plus closing outstanding claims (including IBNR) minus opening outstanding claims
Claims paid during the year only
e: Incurred claims capture the cost of claims belonging to the period, whether paid or still outstanding, by adjusting paid claims for the movement in provisions.

t: A rate revision is being prepared for a health product. Historical incurred claims are ₹60 crore; medical inflation is 8% per annum and the rates will apply two years later than the midpoint of the experience period. The trended losses are approximately:
'Merit rating' in motor insurance is exemplified by:
o: Rating on the basis of vehicle colour
No Claim Bonus and malus loadings based on the individual's claim record
e: Merit rating adjusts the class rate for the individual's own experience; NCB rewards claim-free years.

t: In a private car policy, the No Claim Bonus applicable after four consecutive claim-free years is:
e: The NCB scale is 20% after one claim-free year, 25% after two, 35% after three, 45% after four and 50% after five or more years.

t: A private car has an IDV of ₹8 lakh and the own-damage rate is 3.2%. The insured is entitled to 25% NCB. The own-damage premium payable (before add-ons and GST) is:
Under IRDAI's 2024 health insurance norms, the maximum waiting period that an insurer may impose for pre-existing diseases is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The maximum PED waiting period was reduced from 48 to 36 months, and the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) was reduced to 60 months.

t: In marine cargo rating, which of the following has the LEAST bearing on the premium rate?
o: Scope of clauses (ICC A, B or C)
Voyage, mode of transport and vessel quality
Nature and packing of the goods
e: Cargo rating depends on commodity, packing, route, conveyance, clauses and claims experience; headcount of the shipper is irrelevant.

t: 'Burning cost' in reinsurance or large-risk pricing refers to:
o: The cost of fire brigade charges
Actual losses (within the layer or class) expressed as a percentage of premium or exposure, used to derive a rate
e: Burning cost = losses ÷ exposure (or premium) over a period; it is then loaded for expenses, profit and fluctuations to arrive at the rate.

t: For a five-year period, an excess of loss layer has suffered losses of ₹2 crore, ₹0, ₹3 crore, ₹1 crore and ₹4 crore against subject premium of ₹100 crore each year. The pure burning cost rate for the layer is:
e: Total layer losses = ₹10 crore over total subject premium ₹500 crore = 2% pure burning cost, before loading.

t: Under the File and Use guidelines, the CEO of the insurer was required to certify that:
o: The product and its documents comply with the Insurance Act, regulations and the insurer's underwriting policy
The product has been approved by the reinsurer
e: The CEO's certificate covers legal and regulatory compliance and adherence to the board-approved underwriting policy; the Appointed Actuary certifies pricing.

t: Which of the following was exempt from the free pricing introduced on 1 January 2007?
e: Motor TP remained under administered pricing because it is compulsory and socially sensitive; the other classes were de-tariffed.

t: Which of the following is an objective of regulatory product filing requirements?
o: To restrict the number of products in the market
To ensure all insurers charge the same premium
To ensure products are fair, viable, clearly worded and not against policyholder interest
e: Filing lets the regulator verify that terms are fair and clear, pricing is sound and the product does not disadvantage policyholders, without fixing uniform prices.

t: In the context of product filing, a 'retail' product is generally understood as one:
o: Designed for individuals and small businesses with standardised terms, as distinct from large commercial risks with negotiated terms
e: Regulatory guidelines distinguish retail products (standard terms, individuals/SMEs) from commercial products where terms are tailored to each risk.

t: As per IRDAI's Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests (2024), the free-look period available to a policyholder for policies with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2024 framework provides a uniform free-look period of 30 days from receipt of the policy document, extended from the earlier 15 days.

topic: Applications of File and Use and Use and File Procedures
t: Which of the following best explains why IRDAI moved towards Use and File?
o: To eliminate the need for an Appointed Actuary
To reduce the number of insurers
To enable faster introduction of innovative products while placing responsibility for product governance on the insurer's board and PMC
e: Use and File balances speed to market with accountability: the insurer self-certifies compliance and the regulator supervises after launch.

topic: Applications of File and Use and Use and File Procedures
t: Which of the following statements about the Product Management Committee (PMC) is INCORRECT?
o: It typically includes the Appointed Actuary
It reviews products before launch under Use and File
It is a committee of the Insurance Ombudsman
It monitors product performance after launch
e: The PMC is an internal committee of the insurer, not of the Ombudsman; it owns product design, pricing sign-off and post-launch review.

t: Which of the following is NOT typically a source of information for the underwriter?
e: Underwriters rely on the proposal, inspection, loss runs, financial statements and industry databases; Ombudsman awards are not an underwriting information source.

t: A quota share treaty of 40% means that:
o: The treaty covers only 40% of the insurer's classes
The insurer retains 40% of claims only
The reinsurer accepts 40% of every risk within the treaty and receives 40% of the premium
The reinsurer pays claims above 40% of sum insured
e: Quota share is proportional: premium and losses on every risk are shared in the fixed percentage, typically with a ceding commission to the insurer.

t: The chief advantage of a surplus treaty over a quota share treaty for the ceding insurer is that:
o: It allows the insurer to retain small risks fully and cede only amounts above its retention on large risks
e: Under surplus, the insurer keeps all premium on risks within retention and cedes only the surplus, giving better premium retention; quota share cedes a share of every risk.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re on every policy, as notified for recent financial years, is:
e: The obligatory cession has been progressively reduced and is notified at 4% of sum insured on each policy, subject to limits specified by IRDAI.

t: Catastrophe (CAT) excess of loss reinsurance protects the insurer against:
o: A single large claim on one risk
Accumulation of many claims from one event, such as a cyclone or earthquake
e: CAT XL responds per event across many policies, unlike per-risk XL which responds per individual risk.

t: Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha policy is intended for enterprises where the total value at risk across all insurable asset classes at one location is:
e: Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha covers micro enterprises up to ₹5 crore; Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha applies from ₹5 crore to ₹50 crore.

t: Under the Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha policy, under-insurance is waived up to:
e: The standard micro-enterprise product waives the condition of average where under-insurance does not exceed 15%, a policyholder-friendly feature of the 2021 standard products.

t: A Machinery Breakdown policy covers:
o: Unforeseen and sudden physical loss or damage to machinery from causes such as defective material, short circuit or operator error, while working or at rest
e: MB insurance responds to mechanical and electrical breakdown; fire perils are excluded (covered under the fire policy) and wear and tear is excluded.

t: Which of the following statements about Motor Third Party liability cover in India is correct?
o: Liability for death or bodily injury to third parties is unlimited, while third-party property damage is limited to ₹7.5 lakh
It covers damage to the insured's own vehicle
It is optional for private cars
It is priced freely by each insurer
e: TP cover is compulsory under the Motor Vehicles Act; death/injury liability is unlimited under the Act while TPPD is capped at ₹7.5 lakh in the standard policy.

t: Under a Personal Accident policy, the benefit for loss of one limb or sight of one eye is generally:
e: Death, loss of two limbs/eyes and permanent total disablement attract 100%; loss of one limb or one eye attracts 50% of the capital sum insured.

t: An insurer's net incurred claims are ₹330 crore on net earned premium of ₹440 crore. The incurred claims ratio is:
e: Incurred claims ratio = 330 ÷ 440 = 75%.

t: Which of the following would NOT improve underwriting profitability?
o: Writing more business at inadequate rates to gain market share
Better risk selection and pricing accuracy
Appropriate reinsurance to smooth large losses
e: Growth at inadequate rates increases losses faster than premium; the other measures all improve the underwriting result.

t: 'Cash-flow underwriting' describes the practice of:
o: Accepting risks at inadequate rates to generate premium for investment income
e: Cash-flow underwriting is a soft-market practice that relies on investment returns; it is risky when interest rates fall or losses rise.

t: The qualifying examination for an individual insurance agent conducted by the Insurance Institute of India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). IC-38 is the agents' pre-recruitment examination; IC-01/02/11/14 are Licentiate papers.

t: The Expenses of Management (including commission) limit prescribed by IRDAI for a general insurer is:
e: IRDAI's EoM regulations cap total expenses of management for general insurers at 30% of gross premium written in India (35% for stand-alone health insurers).

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) framework, an insurer must communicate its decision on a proposal within:
o: 15 days of receipt of the proposal or any requisitioned information
e: The regulations require insurers to process proposals and convey their decision within 15 days of receiving the proposal or the last required document.

t: When a surveyor is appointed for a general insurance claim, the surveyor's report must ordinarily be submitted within:
e: IRDAI's 2024 claims timelines require the surveyor to submit the report within 15 days, with the insurer deciding the claim within 7 days of receiving the report.

topic: Research and Development in Underwriting, Rating and Product Innovation
t: Which of the following is a key underwriting challenge posed by climate change for Indian property insurers?
o: Increased frequency and severity of flood, cyclone and other natural catastrophe losses, requiring better CAT modelling and accumulation control
e: Rising NatCat losses strain traditional pricing based on past experience; insurers need CAT models, zonal accumulation limits and adequate CAT reinsurance.

t: 'Straight-through processing' (STP) in underwriting means:
o: Manual review of every proposal by a senior underwriter
Automated acceptance and policy issue of proposals that meet pre-set rules, without manual intervention
Processing proposals only at head office
e: STP uses rule engines to auto-underwrite standard risks (e.g. private cars, retail health), freeing underwriters for complex or exceptional cases.
